The tour includes a visit to Lima Cathedral, the city's principal church, known for its colonial architecture, richly decorated interiors and collection of religious art. Next, you will visit the Santo Domingo Monastery, home to picturesque courtyards, a historic library and works of art. The tour concludes at Casa Aliaga, one of the oldest residences in South America, with period interiors, antique furniture and inviting inner courtyards.

The tour begins at Love Park in Miraflores, overlooking the Pacific Ocean. You will then drive past Huaca Huallamarca, a pre-Inca administrative and religious center in San Isidro. It is a separate archaeological site and should not be confused with Huaca Pucllana.

The Presidential Palace and City Hall stand on the main square. The itinerary includes a visit to Lima Cathedral; if the cathedral is closed, the Museum of Art of Lima (MALI) is visited instead. Visits to both are not promised.

The walk then continues to the Santo Domingo Monastery, associated with the history of Saint Martin de Porres and Saint Rose of Lima.

The tour begins at Love Park in the Miraflores district, overlooking the Pacific Ocean. The route then continues to Huaca Pucllana, a ceremonial center of the Lima culture.

Next, you will head to the Main Square, where the Presidential Palace and City Hall are located. The itinerary also includes Lima Cathedral and the Santo Domingo Monastery, associated with the history of Saint Martin de Porres and Saint Rose of Lima.

The route reveals several distinct sides of the city: modern Miraflores, pre-Columbian sites and Lima's colonial center.
